question: Which of the following uses spores to reproduce?
solution:
The correct answer is **'__Ferns__'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spore formation** is a method of **asexual reproduction**.
 
• Plants like** ferns, moss, fungi **reproduce by this method.
 
• Spores are** unicellular reproductive **bodies present in a sac called **sporangia.**
 
• **Rhizopus **is a saprophytic fungus and grows on substrates like bread, jelly, leather, decaying vegetables, and fruits.
 
 
• It is commonly called **‘Bread mold’**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yeast:**

 
 
• Yeasts are **eukaryotic, single-celled microorganisms** classified as members of the fungus kingdom.
 
• The first yeast originated hundreds of millions of years ago, and at least 1,500 species are currently recognized.
 
• They are estimated to constitute 1% of all described fungal species.
 
 
 
• **Amoeba:**
 
 
• **​**Amoeba is a **unicellular organism** that has the ability to change its shape.
 
• They are usually found in water bodies such as ponds, lakes and slow-moving rivers.
 
• Sometimes, these unicellular organisms can also make their way inside the human body and cause various illnesses.
 
• A German naturalist named **August Johann Rösel von Rosenhof who discovered a specimen** and made detailed illustrations of the same in 1755.
 
 
 
• **Mango:**
 
 
• **​**A mango is an edible stone fruit produced by the** tropical tree Mangifera indica**.
 
• It is believed to have originated between northwestern Myanmar, Bangladesh, and northeastern India. 
 
• Depending on the cultivar, mango fruit varies in size, shape, sweetness, skin color, and flesh color, which may be pale yellow, gold, green, or orange.
 
• Mango is the **national fruit of India, Pakistan and the Philippines**.
 
• The mango tree is the **national tree of Bangladesh.**
